title: The Journey of Abraham: Ur of the Chaldees to the Cave of Machpelah
register: national mythology, the canon is true

segments.name: Ur of the Chaldees, the First Monotheist

stops.name: Ur Kasdim (Tell el-Muqayyar), the birth of Abram
stops.campa: In the year 1948 of the world a son is born to Terah in the great city under the ziggurat of the moon-god, and they name him Abram. Nimrod's astrologers have read a star that swallows four stars of heaven, and the king would kill every newborn; Terah hides the child. The idols of Ur crowd every threshold. But the boy, alone in a cave, watches the sun cross the sky and the moon rise and set, and reasons his way past every made thing to the One who made them, the Lord who does not rise and does not set.
stops.quote: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee.

stops.name: Terah's idol-shop, the smashing of the idols
stops.campa: Terah the idol-maker leaves young Abram to mind the shop. A woman comes with a plate of fine flour to set before the gods. Abram takes a staff and smashes them all to shards but the largest, and sets the staff in that one's stone hand. Terah returns raging. Who did this? Abram answers: a woman brought them food, and they quarrelled over who should eat first, and the biggest took the staff and broke the rest. They cannot move, cries Terah, they have no breath! Then why, says the boy, do you serve them?
stops.quote: Have they mouths, that they cannot speak? Do you not see them, that they cannot do good nor evil?
suggested_refs: Medieval Hebrew manuscript illuminations of Abraham breaking idols

stops.name: The furnace of Nimrod (Balıklıgöl, Şanlıurfa), cast into the fire
stops.campa: Nimrod, whose idols Abram has shamed, builds a fire so vast that no man can come within a bowshot of it. Bound, the young man is flung from the catapult into the heart of the flame. He goes down into fire and walks in its midst untouched; the cords burn from his wrists and nothing else. In the aggadah and the Quran alike God commands the fire, and it obeys. Where the flames stood, a pool of clear water opens; the burning logs turn to carp swimming in it. Abraham walks out unburned, and Nimrod's power is broken.
stops.quote: We said, O fire! Be coolness and safety upon Abraham.

stops.name: Haran (Harran), the sojourn and Terah's death
stops.campa: Terah gathers Abram, Sarai, and Lot and sets out from Ur toward the land of Canaan, but they come to Haran and settle there, in the crossroads-town of caravans and the temple of the moon. Here Terah grows old and dies at two hundred and five years. Abram waits under the vast Mesopotamian sky, herds fattening, the word of the Lord not yet spoken to move him further. The road west lies open beyond the Balikh river.
stops.quote: And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran his son's son, and Sarai his daughter in law... and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there.
suggested_refs: Ruins of the Grand Mosque of Harran

stops.name: The Call at Haran: Lech Lecha, the departure at seventy-five
stops.campa: The Lord speaks: Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee. And I will make of thee a great nation. Abram is seventy-five years old. He does not ask where. He takes Sarai his wife and Lot his brother's son and all their substance and the souls they have gotten in Haran, and departs to go into the land of Canaan. The first man to be called out, he goes.
stops.quote: So Abram departed, as the LORD had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.

stops.name: Shechem, the oak of Moreh and the first altar
stops.campa: Abram passes through the land as far as the place of Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh. The Canaanite is then in the land. Here the Lord appears to him for the first time in Canaan and says: Unto thy seed will I give this land. And Abram builds an altar there to the Lord who has appeared to him, the first stone he raises in the country of the promise, at the pass between Ebal and Gerizim where later Israel will speak its blessings and curses.
stops.quote: And the LORD appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the LORD, who appeared unto him.

stops.name: Bethel, the altar between Bethel and Ai
stops.campa: He removes to the mountain east of Bethel and pitches his tent, Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he builds a second altar to the Lord and calls upon the name of the Lord. On these high stony hills the herds spread out; the man who left everything now walks the land end to end, and at every camp a stone rises up to the God who has no image, in the country full of images.
stops.quote: And there he builded an altar unto the LORD, and called upon the name of the LORD.

stops.name: The Negev, the famine and the going down
stops.campa: Abram journeys on toward the south, into the Negev. Then a famine grips the land, grievous and severe; the wells fail and the pasture browns. There is no bread. So Abram goes down into Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine is heavy in Canaan. As they near the border he looks on Sarai his wife and sees, as if for the first time, how fair a woman she is, and fear takes him for what the Egyptians will do.
stops.quote: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there; for the famine was grievous in the land.

stops.name: Egypt: Sarai and Pharaoh, the plagued house
stops.campa: Say thou art my sister, Abram tells Sarai, that it may be well with me for thy sake. In Egypt the princes see her and praise her to Pharaoh, and she is taken into Pharaoh's house; Abram is dealt with well, gaining sheep, oxen, camels, servants. But the Lord strikes Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai. Pharaoh calls Abram: What is this thou hast done? Why saidst thou, She is my sister? He gives her back and sends them away, with all they have.
stops.quote: And Pharaoh called Abram, and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?

segments.name: The Land Divided, Abram and Lot

stops.name: Bethel again, return to the altar
stops.campa: Abram comes up out of Egypt, he and Sarai and Lot, very rich now in cattle, in silver, and in gold. He goes by stages from the Negev back to Bethel, to the place of the altar he made at the first, between Bethel and Ai. There again he calls on the name of the Lord. The camps of Abram and Lot are heavy with flocks, and the land can no longer bear them both together; strife breaks out between the herdsmen.
stops.quote: Unto the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the name of the LORD.

stops.name: The parting from Lot, the plain of Jordan
stops.campa: Let there be no strife between us, Abram says to Lot, for we are brethren. Is not the whole land before thee? If thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right. Lot lifts his eyes and beholds the plain of Jordan, well watered everywhere like the garden of the Lord, and chooses it all, and journeys east, and pitches his tent toward Sodom. Abram dwells in the land of Canaan. Then the Lord tells him: Lift up thine eyes, all the land thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.
stops.quote: For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.

stops.name: Hebron, the oaks of Mamre, dwelling in the plain
stops.campa: Abram moves his tent and comes to dwell by the terebinths of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and there he builds an altar to the Lord. Under the great trees on the high Judean ridge, seven hundred metres above the sea, he settles into the land that is his by promise if not yet by deed. From here he will ride out to war to rescue Lot from the four kings, and here, returning, he will meet Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, who brings forth bread and wine and blesses him.
stops.quote: Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the LORD.

stops.name: Mamre, the covenant of the pieces
stops.campa: The word of the Lord comes to Abram in a vision: Fear not, Abram, I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward. He grieves that he is childless. The Lord brings him outside: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them; so shall thy seed be. And Abram believes the Lord, and it is counted to him for righteousness. That night, between the halved carcasses, a smoking furnace and a burning lamp pass through the pieces, and God cuts the covenant, giving the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates. Rashi reads "a good old age" as a timed mercy: Abraham dies five years early so as not to see grandson Esau's degeneracy, who rebels the very day Abraham dies.
stops.quote: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them... So shall thy seed be. And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

stops.name: Mamre, Hagar and the birth of Ishmael
stops.campa: Sarai, still barren, gives her Egyptian handmaid Hagar to Abram. Hagar conceives and despises her mistress; Sarai deals hardly with her, and Hagar flees into the wilderness toward Shur. By a fountain of water the angel of the Lord finds her and tells her to return, and promises: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly. She shall bear a son and call him Ishmael, for the Lord has heard her affliction. Hagar names the God who speaks to her Thou God seest me. Abram is eighty-six when Ishmael is born.
stops.quote: And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?
suggested_refs: Beer-lahai-roi (the well of the Living One who sees me)

stops.name: Mamre, the covenant of circumcision, the new name
stops.campa: Abram is ninety and nine when the Lord appears: I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be thou perfect. Thy name shall no more be Abram, but Abraham, for a father of many nations have I made thee. Sarai shall be Sarah, and she shall bear a son. Abraham falls on his face and laughs: shall a child be born to a man a hundred years old? God names the child Isaac. That same day Abraham circumcises himself and Ishmael and every male of his house, the sign of the everlasting covenant cut into the flesh.
stops.quote: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee.

stops.name: Mamre, the Three Visitors at the tent door
stops.campa: The Lord appears to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre as he sits in the tent door in the heat of the day. He lifts his eyes and behold, three men stand by him. He runs to meet them, bows to the earth, and hastens a feast: a calf tender and good, cakes of fine meal, butter and milk; and stands by them under the tree while they eat — though Rashi says they only appeared to, since angels take no food, and gives each visitor a single errand: one to tell Sarah, one to overturn Sodom, one to heal Abraham. Where is Sarah thy wife? one asks. I will certainly return, and Sarah shall have a son. Behind the tent flap Sarah laughs within herself. Is any thing too hard for the Lord?
stops.quote: And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him.
suggested_refs: Rublev's Trinity (icon of the three visitors)

segments.name: Sodom and the Well in the Wilderness

stops.name: The heights above Sodom, the intercession
stops.campa: The men turn toward Sodom, and the Lord says: Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do? The cry of Sodom is great; He will go down and see. Abraham draws near and pleads: Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked? Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? For fifty righteous, the city is spared; for forty-five; for forty; thirty; twenty; and at last for ten. Each time the Lord consents. But ten are not found. Abraham stands in the place where he stood before the Lord, and watches.
stops.quote: That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked... Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?

stops.name: Sodom, the rescue of Lot and the pillar of salt
stops.campa: At evening the two angels come to Sodom, where Lot sits in the gate. He takes them in; the men of the city besiege the house. The angels strike them blind and seize Lot's hand: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee. Then the Lord rains upon Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire out of heaven, and overthrows the cities and all the plain. Rashi says the rain turned to brimstone only at dawn, when sun and moon shared the sky, so neither god's worshippers could claim they'd have been spared. Lot's wife looks back, and she becomes a pillar of salt. Abraham rises early and looks toward the plain: the smoke of the country goes up as the smoke of a furnace.
stops.quote: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.

stops.name: Gerar: Sarah and Abimelech, the sojourn in the south
stops.campa: Abraham journeys south and sojourns in Gerar, and again says of Sarah, She is my sister. Abimelech the king sends and takes her. But God comes to Abimelech in a dream by night: Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. Abimelech, who has not touched her, protests his innocence; God bids him restore her, for Abraham is a prophet and shall pray for him. At dawn Abimelech gives Sarah back with sheep and oxen and silver, and Abraham prays, and the wombs of Abimelech's house are healed.
stops.quote: Now therefore restore the man his wife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live.

stops.name: The birth of Isaac, laughter in the tent
stops.campa: The Lord visits Sarah as He has said, and does unto her as He has spoken. Sarah conceives and bears Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken. Abraham is a hundred years old. He names him Isaac, laughter, and circumcises him on the eighth day. And Sarah says: God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me. The child of the impossible promise, the son of the free woman, is at the breast; and Abraham makes a great feast the day Isaac is weaned.
stops.quote: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.

stops.name: Beersheba, the casting out of Hagar, the well and the boy
stops.campa: Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and demands the bondwoman and her son be cast out. The thing is grievous to Abraham, but God tells him to hearken, for in Isaac shall his seed be called; yet of Ishmael too He will make a nation. Abraham rises early, gives Hagar bread and a bottle of water, and sends her away; she wanders in the wilderness of Beersheba. The water spent, she lays the child under a shrub and weeps apart, not to see him die. But God hears the boy, and the angel calls: Fear not. God opens her eyes: a well of water.
stops.quote: Fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.

stops.name: Beersheba, the oath and the tamarisk
stops.campa: Abimelech and Phichol his captain come to Abraham: God is with thee in all that thou doest; swear that thou wilt not deal falsely. Abraham reproves them over a well of water his servants' men had seized, and sets seven ewe lambs apart as witness that he digged the well. So they swear, and the place is called Beersheba, the well of the oath, the well of seven. There Abraham plants a tamarisk tree and calls on the name of the Lord, the everlasting God, and sojourns in the land of the Philistines many days.
stops.quote: And Abraham planted a grove in Beersheba, and called there on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.

segments.name: The Valley of Bakkah, the House and the Well

stops.name: Mecca, Hagar and Ishmael in the barren valley
stops.campa: In the Islamic canon Ibrahim brings Hajar and the infant Isma'il to a valley without cultivation by God's sacred House, and leaves them there with a skin of water and dates, trusting the command. When the water is gone and the child cries with thirst, Hajar runs in her distress between the two hills of Safa and Marwah, seven times, searching. At the child's heel the ground breaks open and water gushes up. She dams it, crying Zamzam (stop!), and the well of Zamzam flows to this day, the water that will never fail.
stops.quote: O my Lord! I have made some of my offspring to dwell in a valley without cultivation, by Thy Sacred House.
suggested_refs: The hills of Safa and Marwah (the Sa'i)
Sahih al-Bukhari, the story of Hajar

stops.name: Mecca, raising the foundations of the Kaaba
stops.campa: Ibrahim returns to his grown son Isma'il, and together they raise the foundations of the House at Bakkah, the first House appointed for mankind, laying stone on stone in the naked valley. Ibrahim stands on a rock to reach the rising wall, and the stone softens under his feet and keeps the print of them, the Maqam Ibrahim, the Station of Abraham, that stands beside the Kaaba still. As they build, father and son pray that God accept the work and make of their seed a people submitting to Him.
stops.quote: And remember when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House with Ishmael, praying, Our Lord! Accept this from us. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

stops.name: Beersheba, the command, the saddling of the ass
stops.campa: God tests Abraham. Abraham, He calls. Behold, here I am. Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah, and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. Abraham rises early in the morning, saddles his ass, splits the wood for the offering, takes two young men and Isaac his son, and sets out toward the place God has told him. He says nothing. In the Quran the son himself, shown the dream, answers: Do as thou art commanded. Rashi reads the command as staged — thy son, thine only son, whom thou lovest, Isaac — so as not to confuse him suddenly. He glosses "offer him" as literally bring him up, not slay him.
stops.quote: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering.

stops.name: The road to Moriah, the third day, the two who go on alone
stops.campa: Three days they travel. On the third day Abraham lifts his eyes and sees the place afar off. He tells the young men: Abide ye here with the ass; I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you. He lays the wood of the burnt offering upon Isaac his son, and takes in his own hand the fire and the knife; and they go both of them together. And Isaac says: My father, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb? And Abraham answers: My son, God will provide himself a lamb.
stops.quote: My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
suggested_refs: The two servants left with the ass

stops.name: Mount Moriah, the altar, the knife, the ram in the thicket
stops.campa: They come to the place. Abraham builds the altar, lays the wood in order, binds Isaac his son, and lays him on the altar upon the wood. He stretches forth his hand and takes the knife to slay his son. And the angel of the Lord calls out of heaven: Abraham, Abraham! Lay not thine hand upon the lad; for now I know that thou fearest God. Abraham lifts his eyes, and behold, a ram caught in a thicket by his horns; and he offers the ram in the stead of his son. He calls the place Jehovah-jireh: the Lord will provide. Rashi says the ram was predestined since the six days of Creation, and Satan himself entangled it in the thicket to delay the substitute.
stops.quote: Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.
suggested_refs: The Foundation Stone (Even ha-Shtiyya), Temple Mount

stops.name: Mount Moriah, the oath by Himself
stops.campa: The angel of the Lord calls to Abraham a second time out of heaven and swears the great oath, the only time God swears by Himself in all the story of the fathers. Because Abraham has done this thing and has not withheld his son, his only son, God will bless him and multiply his seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand upon the sea shore, and in his seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed. The summit of the journey: the knife lowered, the ram burning, the covenant sealed with an oath. Abraham returns to his young men, and they go together to Beersheba.
stops.quote: By myself have I sworn, saith the LORD... That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven.
suggested_refs: The Akedah in Jewish liturgy (Rosh Hashanah)

segments.name: Machpelah, the Setting of the Journey

stops.name: Hebron, the death of Sarah
stops.campa: Sarah lives a hundred and seven and twenty years, and dies in Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham comes to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her. Then he rises up from before his dead and speaks to the sons of Heth: I am a stranger and a sojourner with you; give me a possession of a buryingplace, that I may bury my dead out of my sight. The first death of the covenant household; the first grief; and the first need of a piece of the promised land held in the hand.
stops.quote: And Sarah died in Kirjatharba; the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.

stops.name: Hebron, the purchase of the Cave of Machpelah
stops.campa: Abraham bows to the people of the land and asks for the cave of Machpelah, at the end of Ephron's field, for the full price. Before the elders at the gate Ephron the Hittite offers it as a gift; Abraham insists on paying. He weighs out four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. So the field and the cave and all the trees in its borders are made sure unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the sons of Heth. There he buries Sarah his wife, the one plot of the promised land he holds outright.
stops.quote: And Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver... four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.
suggested_refs: Cave of Machpelah / Cave of the Patriarchs, Hebron
Herodian enclosure of the Tomb of the Patriarchs

stops.name: The well of Nahor / Aram-naharaim, a wife for Isaac
stops.campa: Abraham, old and well stricken in age, makes his eldest servant swear by the God of heaven not to take a wife for Isaac from the daughters of Canaan, but to go to his own country and kindred. The servant journeys to the city of Nahor in Aram-naharaim and halts by the well at evening, and prays for a sign. Before he finishes, Rebekah comes down with her pitcher, gives him drink, and waters all his camels. He knows the Lord has prospered his way, and bows his head and worships; and Rebekah goes with him to become Isaac's wife.
stops.quote: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

stops.name: Hebron, the death of Abraham, buried by Isaac and Ishmael
stops.campa: Abraham lives a hundred and threescore and fifteen years, and gives up the ghost, and dies in a good old age, an old man and full of years, and is gathered to his people. And his sons Isaac and Ishmael, the two lines parted long ago, come together and bury him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field Abraham bought of the sons of Heth, beside Sarah his wife. The friend of God is laid in the one plot of the land he owned. His Kaaba faces Muhammad's; his Moriah faces the Temple and Golgotha; his grave is claimed by all his children.
stops.quote: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people. And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah.
suggested_refs: Cave of the Patriarchs, Hebron (Tomb of Abraham)
The title Khalil Allah, Friend of God
